parts: Villus lamina propria core | continuous context

stages.name: Function 1 · Apical entry
stages.note: Absorption begins at the lumen-facing enterocyte surface. The brush border is an apical specialization of these cells; goblet cells supply mucus. The whole villus is not a microvillus. Cell and apical-detail dimensions are enlarged teaching samples. No nutrient particles or transporters are rendered.

stages.name: Function 2 · Blood route
stages.note: The epithelial covering is peeled for teaching, not physiologically absent. Water-soluble digestion products pass through enterocytes, across the villus interstitium, into nearby capillaries and venous drainage. Follow the capillary network and venous mucosal branches toward submucosal venules; continuation to the liver is outside this crop. Red-to-blue is a static route cue, not measured oxygen saturation or velocity. The arterial route supplies tissue rather than receiving absorbed nutrients.

stages.name: Function 3 · Lipid route
stages.note: The epithelial covering is peeled for teaching, not physiologically absent. Enterocytes package much absorbed long-chain dietary lipid into chylomicrons. These leave the epithelial basal side, cross villus interstitium and enter the central lacteal, then lymphatic collectors; systemic return is outside the crop. Not all lipid takes this route. Adjacent smooth muscle can assist lacteal drainage: this mechanism has direct mouse imaging evidence, not human timing or amplitude calibration. Hidden epithelium in the next exploration is a teaching peel, not an absorptive hole.

stages.name: Function 4 · Ileal uptake
stages.note: The distal ileum absorbs intrinsic-factor-bound vitamin B12 by receptor-mediated endocytosis and reclaims bile acids using the ileal sodium-dependent bile-acid transporter. These are enterocyte mechanisms; the receptors, ion gradients and molecular packaging are annotation-only. This crop does not prove terminal-ileal transporter distribution, normal uptake rate or a deficiency.

stages.name: Function 5 · Sampling surface
stages.note: Compare the villous absorptive surface with the follicle-associated epithelium over a Peyer-patch dome. The dome lacks villi and crypts; M cells are a minority population among follicle-associated enterocytes. Luminal antigen uptake by M cells begins on their apical surface. Antigen is not visualized and the whole dome is not M-cell epithelium.

stages.name: Function 6 · Basal delivery
stages.note: View from below into the basolateral pocket beneath an M cell. Transcytosis carries selected luminal material through the epithelial cell to this immune-cell interface. The lymphocyte examples occupy the pocket; they are not intracellular M-cell contents. The displayed cells are generic representatives, not evidence of a particular antigen-presenting subtype. The pocket is enlarged and neighbouring tissue is hidden for teaching.

stages.name: Function 7 · Lymphoid response
stages.note: After sampling, antigen interacts with immune populations beneath the follicle-associated epithelium. The follicle and germinal centre support B-cell responses; activation, proliferation and affinity selection are annotation-only. Do not draw an obligatory M-cell → dendritic cell → T-cell → germinal-centre pipeline: direct M-cell-to-B-cell antigen sampling was demonstrated in a mouse study. The model does not resolve immune subtypes, interfollicular T zones, IgA homing or class-switch locations.

stages.name: Function 8 · Coordinated motility
stages.note: Longitudinal and circular smooth muscle act in distinct directions, with the myenteric plexus between them. Peristalsis coordinates contraction behind contents and relaxation ahead to propel and mix them. This is a cropped wall, without an intact bowel circumference or bolus: no deformation, propagating wave, neuron firing or pacemaker rate is simulated. Separation would misrepresent active contraction.

stages.name: Function 9 · Local mucosal control
stages.note: Distinguish local mucosal movement and secretion/absorption regulation from whole-wall propulsion. The submucosal plexus lies in submucosa, and villus muscle lies beside the lacteal. Mouse imaging supports contractile assistance to lacteal drainage; simple villus piston motion is an incomplete explanation. The model preserves anatomical position without showing a measured neural connection or continuous cellular chain from muscularis mucosae into each villus.

stages.name: Function 10 · Barrier renewal
stages.note: Paneth apical granules face the crypt lumen; the crypt-base stem-cell identity is a color/annotation convention, not visible Lgr5 expression. Inspect a coronal/model-z section at z=-0.225 (5% of block width), retain the positive-z/far half, and distinguish epithelial wall from gland lumen. Epithelial renewal supports the absorptive barrier, but no mitosis, cell migration, secretion or assay is simulated. Imported GLB has no authored corner-cut planes; set the single-plane section manually after selecting this view.

sources.title: University of Basel: Ileum, Human 2
sources.relevance: Human H&E relationship evidence: dome without villi or crypts; minority M cells; Paneth granules and muscular/plexus locations. Not morphometry.

sources.title: NIDDK: Your Digestive System & How it Works
sources.relevance: Authoritative human-level digestion/absorption and peristalsis explanation; no crop-specific rates.

sources.title: Choe et al. 2015: Intravital imaging of intestinal lacteals unveils lipid drainage through contractility
sources.relevance: Primary mouse imaging shows epithelial uptake, interstitial distribution and lacteal drainage with adjacent muscle contraction. Mechanistic support, not measured human kinetics.

sources.title: NIH ODS: Vitamin B12 Health Professional Fact Sheet
sources.relevance: Distal-ileal receptor-mediated uptake of intrinsic-factor-bound B12; receptors absent from geometry.

sources.title: Oelkers et al. 1997: Primary bile acid malabsorption caused by SLC10A2 mutations
sources.relevance: Primary human genetic and transporter-expression experiments establish ileal sodium-dependent bile-acid reclamation; no expression map is rendered.

sources.title: Hase et al. 2009: Uptake through GP2 of FimH-positive bacteria by M cells
sources.relevance: Primary molecular uptake/transcytosis mechanism; GP2/FimH are annotation-only, not all antigens use this route.

sources.title: Komban et al. 2019: Activated Peyer-patch B cells sample antigen directly from M cells
sources.relevance: Primary mouse study supports direct antigen-specific M-cell–B-cell sampling and SED-to-GC migration; invalidates a single obligatory dendritic-cell-only transport sequence.

limitations: No mesh, NPZ arrays or application were loaded. No rendering or heavy processing was run.
Camera geometry is inherited from the delivered candidate sidecar; visibility and narrative are newly proposed, not visually accepted.
Existing originals remain read-only; delivered candidate is never silently installed.
Six villi, nine crypts and two follicles are representative counts; 1500 micrometres/model-unit is nominal; cellular detail, granules, microfolds and pockets are pedagogically magnified.

The native UI uses a Views menu when total views exceed 10, so stage notes are also supplied in FUNCTION-GUIDE.md. The function_teaching field is archival content; native cameras provide actual behavior.
